A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain 60 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Text, equations, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B report original kernel-regression simulations and LLM pre-training experiments, including evaluation of FSL-optimized learning-rate schedules.

after.justification: V4 retains the original simulations, LLM loss-trajectory fitting and prediction results, and learning-rate schedule comparisons in Section 6 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The SGD update, intrinsic-time transformation, final FSL formulations, and numerical schedule-optimization procedure are retained. Section 4.4 corrects their mathematical derivation without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic power-law kernel-regression tasks and LLM pre-training coverage. Section 6 and Appendix B add no datasets, tasks, or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same schedules: cosine/WSD/cyclic for kernel trajectories, constant/exponential/WSD for scaling, and cosine/WSD/8-1-1 for LLM experiments. The additional WSD variants in Appendix B are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported fitting protocols, metrics, model sizes, and training budgets are unchanged. For example, the QwenMoE comparison still uses 1B parameters, 20B tokens, 33,907 steps, and batch size 288.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the analyses varying task difficulty and capacity, model size and architecture, training duration, WSD decay ratios, and final learning rates. Figures 3–9 contain no added or removed analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 1 retains its 1,000-run and 200-run averaging descriptions and error bars; Appendix B.1 retains its 200-independent-run descriptions. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical-estimation procedure changes.

E6.justification: The plotted results, rankings, and reported values are unchanged. Figures 4 and 5 retain RMSE values 0.01851 and 0.03792, respectively, and Figure 8 retains the approximately 0.01 loss-gap finding.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 removes an extra λ_j from the coordinate-variance integral, inserts E[q_j(z)], changes λ_j² to λ_j in Eq. (14), and replaces E[E_t] with E[E_z] inside Eq. (15). Appendix A.3 changes δ's range from (0,1) to (0,s), removes the unsupported continuity qualifier from Definition A.1, and states RKHS uniqueness. These are local corrections and refinements; the main theorem statements and scaling bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about full-trajectory FSLs, learning-rate schedule efficiency, and practical LLM loss prediction and schedule design.

C2.justification: The signal-learning/noise-forgetting interpretation and WSD mechanism are unchanged. The random-feature caveat for s > 1 in Section 4.3 and the future-work boundaries in Section 7 are also retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same simulation details, fitting objectives, Adam learning rates, projected-gradient optimization settings, and training specifications. No implementation or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds Pan, Wang, and Li's 2025 work, Understanding LLM behaviors via compression: Data generation, knowledge acquisition and scaling laws, as reference [48]. Existing research positioning is retained; subsequent citation-number shifts are bookkeeping.

P1.justification: V4 expands the coordinate-noise explanation in Section 4.4 and revises the kernel/RKHS background in Appendix A.3. Other edits concern local wording, capitalization, and notation; the document's overall organization is unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes its legend from 'SGD excess risk' and 'Functional Scaling Law' to 'SGD results' and 'FSL prediction'; the plotted content is unchanged. Local reflow moves Eq. (15) from page 10 to page 11 and shifts bibliography entries.

improvement.justification: V4 corrects erroneous factors and expectation/time arguments in Section 4.4, aligning the proof outline with the Volterra relation already present in Appendix C. The δ-range correction in Appendix A.3 further improves mathematical precision. These repairs provide a limited overall improvement while the substantive theorems and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
